Guidance & outlook: This year-end performance provides a steady starting point as we move into FY27. *Note: For FY26, we delivered revenue of INR880.7 8 crores and for the fourth quarter FY26 revenue stood at INR418.39 crores and PAT at INR194.26 crores.

Indiabulls Limited April 29, 2026 Going back to the FY26 numbers, we sold about 21.6 lakh square feet throughout the year, and Q4 FY26 marks the first quarter of real estate revenue recognition in the company's books.

What follows is not a one-time event, but this is the beginning of a sustained earnings cycle, with real estate profits in FY27 expected to grow at least 2x from what it is today, and FY28 will be at least 3x from what it is here.
Growth & demand: This is no longer a pipeline story but an active contracted revenue engine, consisting of both owned projects and signed up with JV partners, with total GDV potential of approximately INR21,000 plus crores and a sellable area of exceeding 1.1 crore lakh square feet, spanning residential, commercial, plotted, and mixed -use development across Gurugram, Mumbai…
Key launch projects in FY26 include Indiabulls Estate and Club Sector 104, the first phase, where over 75% of inventory has been already sold .
Taken together, the company's GDP potential stands at INR21,000 plus crores, representing the cumulative value of launch projects plus current year planned launches and the future launch pipeline.
Margins & costs: We are just in the mode of collection, so the first year will go in getting adjusting the collections to the cost of our acquisition, and then the profits will roll in from ARC, which will start from next year.
Capex & expansion: So typically, the our investment in the US company was done at $30 million, where the company was valued at $30 million, and we did it about 6 months back.
Balance sheet & cash: The balance sheet is net cash positive with no loss-making entities, no hidden liabilities, and no legacy impairment beyond the ones which could occur in the normal operational business.
We are entering FY2027 with a net cash positive balance, zero loss-making entities, and a strong real estate pipeline.
So I mean, it's likely that there would be high receivables, but the numbers would not reflect that, I mean, the PAT.
Risks & challenges: However, over time, we recognized that fintech lending to faceless customers suffers from structurally weak unit economics, challenges in underwriting and collection, and an inability to generate su stainable profits.
Financial services will continue to build steadily, adding to the base in a capital -efficient and low-risk manner.

Growth momentum remained strong throughout the year, with real GDP expanding 7.8% in Q1 and accelerating to 8.2% in Q2 of FY2025- 26, up from 5.6% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year, taking H1 FY2026 growth to 8%, compared with 6.1% in H1 FY2024-25.

Following a record ₹9.9 lakh crore in issuances during FY2024-25, total corporate bond issuances for FY2025-26 were estimated to reach close to ₹11 lakh crore, a fresh all-time high, with Q1 FY2026 issuance alone hitting a four-year high of ₹3.27 lakh crore.

During FY2025-26, we launched three marquee residential developments across high-growth micro-markets in NCR representing a combined saleable area of 28.67 lakh square feet and an estimated GDV of ₹3,393 crore.
Real estate continued to anchor growth, contributing around ₹143 crore at the earnings level in Q4FY26; supported by strong pipeline visibility.
Margins & costs: As per the Economic Survey 2025- 26, average headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation for April-December 2025 came in at just 1.7%, the lowest since the inception of the CPI series, driven by sustained disinflation in food and fuel, which together constitute over 52% of the consumption basket.

India recorded one of the sharpest declines in headline inflation among major emerging economies during 2025, at about 1.8 percentage points, even as growth remained robust at 8% in H1 FY2026, reflecting non-inflationary expansion rather than overheating.

Inflation troughed at an eight-year low before edging up modestly later in the year, with December 2025 inflation at 1.33%, still comfortably below the RBI's 2-6% tolerance band; the RBI accordingly projected full-year FY2026 inflation at around 2.1%.

This performance was bolstered by the Government's continued focus on capital expenditure, tax simplification, and structural reforms, including Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate rationalisation effective from September 2025, which directly impacted pricing across roughly 11% of the CPI basket.

Gross GST collections during April-December 2025 stood at ₹17.4 lakh crore, registering a year-on-year growth of 6.7%, reflecting steady revenue buoyancy alongside continued front-loading of capital expenditure on infrastructure.

It is in the Members interest to claim any un-cashed dividends and for future, opt for Electronic Clearing Service, so that dividends paid by the Company are credited to the Members account on time.

The rate remained unchanged at 5.25% through subsequent policy reviews into FY2026-27, as the central bank adopted a cautious, data-driven approach amid a weakening rupee and evolving geopolitical risks.
